title: Multi-Timeframe Thinking
hook: Higher timeframes give context. Lower timeframes reveal detail.

launchpad.outcome: Explain why zooming in changes what you can see, not what's actually happening.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What's the risk in forming your entire directional bias off the 1-minute chart alone?

slides.kicker: Every timeframe has a job. You just don't know what it is yet.
slides.body:
Higher timeframes give you context: the bigger picture of what price is doing. Lower timeframes reveal detail: the smaller moves inside that picture.

Later in the Academy, you'll learn exactly how AGHF assigns a specific job to each timeframe. For now, just get comfortable with the idea that they're telling different parts of the same story.

slides.title: Tap the timeframes in the order you'd generally check them
slides.body: Biggest picture first, most zoomed in last.
slides.successFeedback: That's the general zoom order: biggest picture first, most detail last. You'll learn the exact job each one does later in the Academy.
slides.failFeedback: Not quite the order: think biggest picture first, most zoomed-in last.

slides.kicker: What's the risk in her thinking?
slides.body: A trader treats every timeframe as if it should give her the same kind of answer.

check.prompt: What's the risk in her thinking?

options.label: There's no risk, all timeframes should always agree perfectly
options.feedback: Timeframes don't have to agree perfectly at every moment.

options.label: She'll get confused when a detailed view and a big-picture view naturally look different
options.why: Exactly. Expecting every timeframe to answer the same question leads to unnecessary confusion.

slides.quote: I'm not going to hand you the whole framework in one lesson. Right now, just notice that a higher timeframe and a lower timeframe are telling you different parts of the same story.

slides.body: Bigger picture, then structure, then detail, in that order.

check.prompt: The clean beginner flow is bigger picture, then structure, then ___ detail last.

options.label: News
options.feedback: News isn't the third step in this flow, entry detail is.

options.label: Guesswork
options.feedback: The whole point of this flow is to remove guesswork, not add it at the end.

options.label: Entry
options.why: Entry detail comes last, after the bigger picture and structure are established.

slides.prompt: Imagine another AGHF member asks: "Why not just trade off the 1-minute chart the whole time?" How would you explain it to them?
slides.modelAnswer: Because the 1-minute chart is built to show detail, not to establish the overall direction of the market. If you only look at the 1M, every small wiggle can feel like a huge signal, when it's really just noise inside a much bigger picture. Checking the higher timeframes first gives you the context to actually understand what the 1M is showing you.

takeaways: Higher timeframes give context; lower timeframes reveal detail.
Zooming in changes what you can see, not what's actually happening.
A messy lower timeframe doesn't erase a clear higher-timeframe read.
remember: Different timeframes, different parts of the same story.
